Trump kicks off Asia tour ahead of major talks with Putin, Xi in China
Published November 17, 2026last updated November 17, 2026
US President Donald Trump is flying into Manila for a Quad meeting before he takes off to China for a much anticipated meet with Russian and Chinese counterparts. Follow live.
What you need to know
- US President Donald Trump set to arrive in Manila on Tuesday amid protests
- Trump to meet leaders of India, Japan and Australia for his first Quad meeting
- Asia tour includes highly-anticipated trilateral meet between Trump, Xi and Putin
Here are the biggest headlines from Trump's Asia tour on Tuesday, November 17:
Canada, China agree to ease tariffs amid trade rows with US
Talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen have produced deals to further reduce tariffs, Ottawa said on Tuesday.
The agreements reflect a growing rapprochement between the two countries after years of strained relations, thanks to trade tensions with Washington leading both Canada and China to seek to reduce dependence on the US.
Read the full story here.
What's on the agenda?
Trump will arrive in Manila later afternoon or early evening. Here's what he's expected to do:
- Meet with Quad leaders — a grouping of US, India, Australia and Japan — for strategic security in the Indo-Pacific
- Signing of a trade deal with Thailand in the wake of the trade war Trump launched in 2025
- A cocktail reception and dinner with other world leaders hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr
- Trump will skip the larger East Asia Summit but join a US-ASEAN 'Special Summit' meant to discuss deepening trade, security and the region's conflicts
- On Wednesday, Trump leaves for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen, China
- There, he will hold a trilateral meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin
Trump set to arrive in Manila amid protests
US President Donald Trump is set to arrive in Manila, Philippines on Tuesday evening for his first meeting of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific countries.
The Asia tour comes as Trump's Republican Party reels from a stunning defeat in the US midterm elections and the Nvidia spy allegations at home.
His administration likely hopes the high-profile meetings of the tour will shift the conversation away from these recent setbacks. That said, the US president is set to be greeted by protesters, angry over the US-Israeli war in the Middle East as well the "Pax Silica" supply chain initiative.
Several miles from the Southeast Asian summit venue in Manila, hundreds of leftist activists, students and indigenous people gathered for a three-day campout against Trump."Trump is a fascist, a warmonger and enabler of brutal, genocidal regimes," rights group Karapatan, one of the groups involved, said in a statement.
The group also accused Trump of pursuing policies that had caused death and destruction worldwide and criticized President Ferdinand Marcos Jr for welcoming him to the Philippines.
Welcome to our coverage
Good morning and welcome to DW's coverage of US President Donald Trump's Asia tour.
Trump is flying into the Philippines to kick off his tour — which he will be hoping makes a positive splash on the global stage and shift attention from his Republican party's deep losses in the recent US midterm elections.
The US President is arriving at the tail end of the ASEAN summit in Manila where he will also join a Quad meeting with the leaders of Japan, Australia and India.
The main attraction, however, comes on Wednesday.
After Manila, Trump will fly to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit where he will have his third face-to-face meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this year. The two will also be joined by Russian President Vladimir Putin for a highly anticipated and controversial trilateral meeting.
Stay tuned for all of this and more!
